about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: never played on the Board or in Defuse. Cambridge formats only, written around the traps B2 First actually sets.

rounds.prompt: 'I'm leaving tomorrow,' she said. She said she ___ the next day.
rounds.note: Present continuous moves back to past continuous.

rounds.prompt: He asked me where ___ the night before.
rounds.note: A reported question keeps statement word order: where I had been.

rounds.prompt: The teacher told us ___ our phones during the test.
rounds.note: tell + object + not to + verb for a negative order.

rounds.prompt: She ___ me that she had already seen the film.
rounds.note: tell + person (told me); say has no person after it (said that).

rounds.prompt: He ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed him.
rounds.note: deny + -ing: he said he hadn't done it.

rounds.prompt: My mum suggested ___ a taxi because it was so late.
rounds.note: suggest + -ing (or suggest that we take) — never suggest to.

rounds.prompt: They asked ___ I could come to the party on Saturday.
rounds.note: Yes/no questions are reported with if or whether.

rounds.prompt: 'Don't touch the oven!' My dad warned me ___ the oven.
rounds.note: warn + object + not to + verb.

rounds.prompt: She apologised ___ late for the meeting.
rounds.note: apologise for + -ing.

rounds.prompt: 'Shall I carry your bag?' he said. He ___ to carry my bag.
rounds.note: offer + to + verb, with no person after offer.

rounds.prompt: He said he would call me ___, but he never did.
rounds.note: tomorrow becomes the following day / the next day.

rounds.prompt: The interviewer asked me what ___ to do after school.
rounds.note: Wh- questions keep statement order and shift back: what I wanted.

rounds.prompt: 'You should revise more,' my teacher said. My teacher ___ me to revise more.
rounds.note: advise + object + to + verb.

rounds.prompt: She reminded me ___ the lights before I left.
rounds.note: remind + object + to + verb.

rounds.prompt: He accused me ___ his charger.
rounds.note: accuse someone of + -ing.

rounds.prompt: 'I've lost my keys,' Ana said. Ana said she ___ her keys.
rounds.note: Present perfect moves back to past perfect: had lost.

rounds.prompt: She asked me ___ I had ever been to London.
rounds.note: A yes/no question is reported with if or whether.

rounds.prompt: He said ___ the match had been cancelled.
rounds.note: say + that + clause.

rounds.prompt: My parents told me not ___ stay out after midnight.
rounds.note: tell + object + not to + verb.

rounds.prompt: The coach insisted ___ us training every day.
rounds.note: insist on + object + -ing.

rounds.prompt: He wanted to know where I ___ bought my trainers.
rounds.note: Past simple in the question (Where did you buy …?) becomes past perfect: had bought.

rounds.prompt: Tom admitted ___ eaten the last piece of cake.
rounds.note: admit + having + past participle, for something before the speaking.

rounds.prompt: She said she was meeting her friends ___ evening.
rounds.note: this evening usually becomes that evening when it's no longer today.

rounds.prompt: The guide warned us ___ to go near the edge.
rounds.note: warn + object + not to + verb.

rounds.prompt: He asked me ___ I was so upset.
rounds.note: A wh- question keeps its question word: why I was so upset.

rounds.prompt: My friend congratulated me ___ passing my driving test.
rounds.note: congratulate someone on + -ing.

rounds.prompt: She threatened ___ call the police if we didn't turn the music down.
rounds.note: threaten + to + verb.

rounds.prompt: The teacher asked us whether we ___ finished the homework yet.
rounds.note: Have you finished …? becomes whether we had finished.

rounds.prompt: When I asked him the time, he said he ___ no idea.
rounds.note: I have no idea → he said he had no idea.

rounds.prompt: She blamed her little sister ___ breaking the vase.
rounds.note: blame someone for + -ing.

rounds.prompt: 'I'll definitely be on time,' said Marco.
rounds.note: promise + to + verb, or promise (that) + would.

rounds.prompt: 'Why don't we go bowling?' said Sara.
rounds.note: suggest + -ing, or suggest (that) we (should) go — never suggest to go.

rounds.prompt: 'Don't forget to bring your passport,' my mum said to me.
rounds.note: remind + object + to + verb.

rounds.prompt: 'I didn't take your phone,' he said.
rounds.note: deny + -ing (or deny that …).

rounds.prompt: 'Where do you live?' the receptionist asked me.
rounds.note: Statement order and a step back in tense: where I lived.

rounds.prompt: 'You broke my sunglasses!' Lucy said to her brother.
rounds.note: accuse someone of + -ing.

rounds.prompt: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said to me.
rounds.note: apologise for + -ing.

rounds.prompt: 'You should see a doctor,' my friend said to me.
rounds.note: advise + object + to + verb.

rounds.prompt: 'Can you help me with my homework?' my sister asked me.
rounds.stem: My sister asked me ___ her with her homework.
rounds.note: can → could, and whether for a yes/no question.

rounds.prompt: 'I won't apologise,' said Leo.
rounds.note: refuse + to + verb: he said he wouldn't.

rounds.prompt: 'Turn off your phones, please,' the teacher said to us.
rounds.note: ask + object + to + verb for a polite request.

rounds.prompt: 'Have you finished your essay?' my teacher asked me.
rounds.stem: My teacher asked me if ___ my essay.
rounds.note: Present perfect → past perfect, statement order.

rounds.prompt: 'I was here yesterday,' he said.
rounds.stem: He said he ___ the day before.
rounds.note: was → had been, here → there, yesterday → the day before.

rounds.prompt: 'You really must try the cake!' Grandma said to me.
rounds.note: insist on + -ing, or insist (that) + clause.

rounds.prompt: 'Be careful, the floor is wet,' the cleaner said to us.
rounds.stem: The cleaner ___ the floor was wet.
rounds.note: warn + object + (that) + clause.

rounds.prompt: 'Don't worry, I'll pay for the tickets,' said Dad.
rounds.note: offer + to + verb.
